paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the rank and errors in BoolQ. The x-axis, labeled 'Rank', has a logarithmic scale, ranging from 4 to 256, with tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, labeled 'Errors (BoolQ)', has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. A single black line with green circular markers represents the data, showing a decrease from approximately 0.25 at a rank of 4 to 0.23 at a rank of 16, followed by an increase to 0.27 at a rank of 64, and further to 0.34 at a rank of 256; error bars around the markers extend from the minimum to the maximum values, indicating variability in the data.
